label: prop:confinement-topological
title: A matrix inequality in the standard representation of $H_3(q)$ (confinement LP evidence)
html:
Let \rho be the standard two-dimensional representation of H_3(q) over the Laurent ring \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}], with q = t^2,

  \rho(\sigma_0) = \begin{pmatrix} q & 1 \\ 0 & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  \rho(\sigma_1) = \begin{pmatrix} -q^{-1} & 0 \\ 1 & q \end{pmatrix},

and put L_+ = \rho(\sigma_0\sigma_1), L_- = \rho(\sigma_1\sigma_0). Then

  L_+^2 + L_-^2 \;\neq\; 2\,L_+ L_- ,

since the (0,0) entries differ: -1 on the left and 2q^2 on the right.

This inequality is the only part proved. It is offered as evidence for the confinement linear program of 14.2.1; the claims that the program over the Gram matrix of H_3(q) at q_0 has optimal value 0, that its optimum lies outside the image of B_3, and that \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 is the unique braid of length \le 6 hitting n_{\mathrm{target}} for both nucleons, are not part of this statement.
